chunks.why: Preface plus Basil painting the portrait; Dorian offstage but exalted as adored, beautiful youth.
Dorian meets Lord Henry; charmed but unsettled by his hedonist creed. Still innocent.
Fatal wish before the finished portrait; learns his tragic parentage. Outwardly fine, soul now mortgaged.
Lord Henry welcomes him into fashionable society; Dorian is the toast of the circle.
Rapturously in love with Sibyl Vane; euphoric, planning to rescue her from the theatre.
Engaged to Sibyl; she is joyful, though Jim's murderous jealousy shadows the scene.
Dorian announces engagement to Basil and Harry, radiant with pleasure; Jim swears vengeance.
Sibyl acts badly; Dorian brutally casts her off; portrait acquires first cruel line.
Sibyl kills herself; Dorian shrugs it off under Harry's influence, chooses eternal youth.
Aestheticizes Sibyl's death, goes to opera; portrait alone bears his shame.
Panics that Basil may see the picture; locks portrait in the old schoolroom to conceal his soul.
Reads the inquest coldly; is poisoned by the yellow book that will shape his life.
Years of decadent connoisseurship; rumors of vice spread; men shun him though wealth shields him.
Broods on ancestors' evil; Basil confronts him with the terrible whispers about his ruined friends.
Shows Basil the corrupted portrait, then stabs him to death in the schoolroom.
Blackmails Alan Campbell into dissolving the body; dines at Lady Narborough's, wildly acting the part.
Burns Basil's coat and bag; opium den; his old name Prince Charming is flung back at him.
James Vane corners him with a pistol; he escapes by his mask of youth but is now hunted.
James Vane shot dead by accident in the coverts; Dorian, terrified then relieved, feels safe.
Stabs the portrait; found dead on the floor, withered and loathsome, knife in his heart.
